focus: Chemicals, plastics and raw-materials trade flows — built while prepping for Tricon Energy's Commercial Development Program

routes.title: Strait of Hormuz closure risk
routes.summary: Iran's restriction of traffic through Hormuz — called by the IEA the largest oil-supply disruption in the history of the global oil market — cut ~20% of global oil supply and major LNG volumes. Ethylene, propylene, benzene and polymer pellets move through Hormuz on dedicated tankers; downstream resin costs rose up to 40% in places. Trade press framing: "Hormuz could reopen tomorrow. Resin still wouldn't arrive for 275 days" — the re-contracting and pipeline-fill lag is itself the story. India is the most exposed buyer (60%+ of oil imports from the Middle East, fast-growing resin-consuming packaging sector).

routes.title: Red Sea avoidance — Cape of Good Hope reroute
routes.summary: Most Asia–Europe tanker and container traffic still routes around the Cape of Good Hope rather than through Suez/Bab-el-Mandeb. Adds 10–14 transit days Asia–Europe; freight rates still +25–40% versus pre-crisis. Chemical tankers specifically carry a 0.5–1.0%-of-vessel-value war-risk premium through the Red Sea corridor.

routes.title: Panama Canal — drought recovery, still tight
routes.summary: Drought-driven draft and transit restrictions have eased versus the acute 2023–2024 crisis, but capacity remains tighter than normal — relevant to any US Gulf Coast-to-Asia petrochemical routing question.

routes.title: China flips from PE/PP importer to exporter
routes.summary: China's PE/PP imports hit record lows in April 2026 while its own PE exports hit record highs (+122% YoY). This structurally squeezes the market US Gulf Coast exporters were counting on, landing right as ~3.3 million tonnes/year of new US PE capacity (Shell, Baystar, Nova, Dow) has come online since 2023 — a demand-side story compounding the transport-side disruptions above.

routes.title: US Gulf Coast new PE capacity chasing a shrinking export pool
routes.summary: ~2 million tonnes/year of new HDPE capacity starting up in Orange, TX by mid-2026 alone, almost entirely aimed at export, on top of 3.3M+ tonnes/year added since 2023 (Shell, Baystar, Nova, Dow) — landing in the same export markets China has just started competing for directly.
